newsitem.title: INDIA: India finance firm seen getting $100 mln funds.
newsitem.headline: India finance firm seen getting $100 mln funds.

text.p: The Infrastructure Development Finance company Ltd (IDFC), a new Indian firm to be incorporated this month, is likely to get $100 million from foreign investors, a top official of the finance ministry said on Friday.
"We have in principle offers (to participate in IDFC equity) of 3.25 billion rupees from non-government Indian financial institutions," Finance secretary Montek Singh Ahluwalia said.
"There are indications of $100 million from foreign investors," Ahluwalia told reporters.
Ahluwalia said multilateral funding agencies such as Asian Development Bank were keen on participating in the new firm.
He was briefing the media after a meeting of the promoters and prospective investors of the new firm. The formation of IDFC was announced by the finance minister in last year's budget.

The initial promoters are the government and the Reserve Bank of India. Representatives of Indian financial institutions, the Unit Trust of India, the country's largest mutual fund and State Bank of India, the largest commercial bank, were present.
IDFC would be incorporated on January 31 with an initial capital of 20 million rupees. The authorised capital is expected to be raised to 10 billion rupees by the year-end.
The government and the Reserve Bank would together have a minority stake in the company, the first Indian institution dedicated to infrastructure financing.
IDFC would prepare a detailed business plan by May 31 to enable prospective investors to decide on investing in its equity, Ahluwalia said.
He said the World Bank indicated it was keen on lending to the institution after it was set up.
"It would be a market-driven company, funding bankable, commercial projects," he said.
He said IDFC would borrow from India and abroad to raise funds for infrastructure financing.
